Author: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
Bench: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 4540 of 2024
Applicant :- Shakil Shah
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Muktesh Kumar Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pradeep Kumar Mishra
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.
Heard Mr. Muktesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and Mr. Pradeep Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the informant.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under Section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.247 of 2020, under Sections 363, 366, 368, 504, 506, 376 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Kerakat, District Jaunpur.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case just to harass the applicant in fact no such incident has taken place as alleged in the impugned FIR.
The applicant has never committed any offence as alleged in the impugned FIR.

sentences.text: Initially the impugned FIR has been lodged by the father of the victim under Sections. 363, 366, 504 and 506 IPC alleging that applicant and other co-accused persons enticed away her minor daughter.

After five months of the alleged incident, the victim was recovered and her statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded in which the victim has stated that she was having love affairs with the applicant for the last two years and she solemnized marriage with the applicant and living together as husband and wife in District Varanasi.

He further submits that earlier after lodging the impugned FIR, the applicant and other co-accused persons including the victim have filed Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.9508 of 2020 before this Court and a Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 08.10.2020 has granted protection till filing of police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.9508 of 2020
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: After investigation, charge sheet was submitted against the applicant and other co-accused persons under Sections 363, 366, 368, 504, 506, 376 IPC and 5/6 POCSO Act and the court below vide order dated 11.12.2023 has taken cognizance against the applicant.

Being aggrieved, the applicant has approached this Court by filing Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.9332 of 2021 before this Court and this Court vide order dated 21.06.2021 granted interim anticipatory bail to the applicant and later on the said anticipatory bail was disposed of directing the applicant to approach before the court below and apply for bail vide order dated 30.11.2022.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.9332 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: In compliance of the said order, the applicant approached before the court below by filing anticipatory bail application, which was rejected by the court below, hence, this application.
The applicant is having no previous criminal history as has been mentioned in paragraph 24 of the affidavit.

He further submits that there is apprehension of imminent arrest of the applicant and in case, the applicant is released on anticipatory bail, he will not misuse the liberty and would co-operate with the trial.
4.

Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicant and have raised a preliminary objection regarding maintainability of the present anticipatory bail application by submitting that the instant anticipatory bail application has been filed under Section 5/6 POCSO Act, which is barred by under Section 438 (6) Cr.P.C.
He has further submitted that victim has also solemnized second marriage with one Ram Sahai.

5. In reply, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that as per high school certificate of the victim, her date of birth is mentioned as 27.09.2003 as well as certificated issued by Municipal Corporation Delhi, the victim is aged about 19 years.
He drawn attention of the Court towards annexure no.6 to the affidavit, which is certificate issued by Office of Chef Medical Office, Jaunpur in which the age of the victim is mentioned as 18 years.

entities.text: Office of Chef Medical Office, Jaunpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, Section 5/6 POCSO Act will not applicable in the present case.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of applicant,
particularly, keeping in mind the statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C, this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail as per the Constitution Bench judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2020 SCC Online SC 98.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2020 SCC Online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.

sentences.text: In the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on anticipatory bail.

Let the applicant-Shakil Shah, involved in the aforesaid case crime be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer during investigation and shall report to the Investigating Officer as and when required for the purpose of conducting investigation.

(ii) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
(iii) The applicant shall not leave the country during the currency of trial without prior permission from the concerned trial Court.
(iv) The applicant shall surrender his passport, if any, to the concerned Court forthwith.
His passport will remain in custody of the concerned Court.
(v) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law to ensure presence of the applicant.

(vi) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail, the Court concerned may take appropriate action in accordance with law and judgment of Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2020 SCC Online SC 98.
(vii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2020 SCC Online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and proceed against his in accordance with law.

8. In default or misuse of any of the conditions, the Public Prosecutor/ Investigating Officer/ first informant-complainant is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
9. With the aforesaid observations/ directions, the application is disposed of.
